'''''Sankhyā: The Indian Journal of Statistics''''' is a quarterly [[Peer review|peer-reviewed]] [[scientific journal]] on [[statistics]] published by the [[Indian Statistical Institute]] (ISI).

It was established in 1933 by [[Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis]], founding director of ISI, along the lines of [[Karl Pearson]]'s ''[[Biometrika]]''.<ref name=obit>{{cite book | first = C. R | last = Rao | author-link = Calyampudi Radhakrishna Rao | year = 1973 | title = Prasantha Chandra Mahalanobis. 1893–1972 | publisher = Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society| volume = 19 | pages=454–492}}</ref> Mahalanobis was the founding [[editor-in-chief]].<ref name=sbrao>{{cite web
| url = http://pib.nic.in/feature/fe0799/f0207991.html
| title = Indian Statistical Institute – A Tradition
| author = S. B. Rao
| author-link = S. B. Rao
| publisher = [[Press Information Bureau]], Government of India
| accessdate = 11 February 2013
}}</ref>

Each volume of ''Sankhya'' consists of four issues, two of them are in Series A, containing articles on theoretical statistics, [[probability theory]], and [[stochastic process]]es, whereas the other two issues form Series B, containing articles on applied statistics, i.e. applied probability, applied stochastic processes, [[econometrics]], and statistical computing.<ref name=sankhya>{{cite web | url = http://sankhya.isical.ac.in/index.html | title = Sankhya Home | accessdate = 11 February 2013}}</ref>

''Sankhya'' is considered as "core journal" of statistics by the [[Current Index to Statistics]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.statindex.org/CIS/news/CIS_core_journals.pdf | page = 3 | title = Core Journal List | publisher = [[Current Index to Statistics]] | accessdate = 11 February 2013 | archive-date = 17 March 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120317033725/http://www.statindex.org/CIS/news/CIS_core_journals.pdf | url-status = dead }}</ref>

== Publication history ==
''Sankhya'' was first published in June 1933. In 1961, the journal split into two series: Series A which focused on mathematical statistics and Series B which focused on statistical methods and applications. A third series, Series C, was added in 1974 and covered sample surveys and quantitative economics in alternating issues. In 1978, the quantitative economics portion became Series D. In 1981, the journal returned to two series when Series B-D were merged. In 2003, Series A and B were recombined into a single journal, but then split again in 2008. ISI began publishing ''Sankhya A'' and ''B'' via [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] in 2010.<ref>{{Cite conference|last=Khatri|first=N.K.|date=October 2009|title=E-Journal Publishing in India: A Case Study of Indian Statistical Institute Publication: Sankhya – The Indian Journal of Statistics|url=http://crl.du.ac.in/ical09/papers/index_files/ical-65_186_390_1_RV.pdf|conference=International Conference on Academic Libraries (ICAL-2009)}}</ref>
